=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py:62-68 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The fallback-env contract test expects an exact YAML substring that the workflow formatting in plan.yml and implement.yml does not satisfy.
  WHY: Reviewers reported pytest will fail because only review_autofix.yml contains the exact string; one reviewer disputed this, but the highest reported severity is major.
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py:85-100 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The implement-loop count assertion expects exactly one literal `CODEX_THREAD_REUSE_MODEL="${MODEL_EDITOR}"`, but the file uses `CODEX_THREAD_REUSE_MODEL="${attempt_model}"` for the main pass.
  WHY: Reviewers said the assertion will fail in CI because it does not match the committed workflow logic.
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py:71-82,103-107 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The contract checks assert `--model "${MODEL_EDITOR}"` is entirely absent from plan.yml and review_apply_fixes.sh, making them brittle to any additional legitimate primary-model codex call.
  WHY: A future valid invocation would fail the tests even if behavior is correct.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1453-1599 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The retry loop and fallback guard hardcode `3` instead of deriving the fallback trigger from the loop bound.
  WHY: Reviewers said changing the retry limit could silently desync the final-attempt fallback behavior.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1182-1184, .github/workflows/implement.yml:2236-2238, scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1598-1600 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The fallback-switch blocks do not validate or escalate if the fallback model itself is invalid, unavailable, or rate-limited; they only echo a message and continue.
  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on severity (one called it nit, two called it major), so use the highest severity; all agree the final attempt can still fail with no extra handling.
- scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:378-380 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new openai/gpt-5.5 catalog entry sets `"priority": 2` and reuses the shared base_instructions blob, which reviewers said may affect model selection or ordering.
  WHY: One reviewer said the priorities are appropriate and another said the lower priority may matter outside the editor path, so this remains a nit-level disagreement.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:426-426 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The telemetry/ledger logging uses the raw MODEL_EDITOR value instead of the per-attempt EDITOR_ATTEMPT_MODEL.
  WHY: The reviewer said fallback attempts would be logged as the primary model, making capacity-failure debugging harder.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: The contract test should reliably assert that the fallback environment variable is present and correctly formatted across all three workflow files, regardless of YAML formatting variations or comment placements.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The exact FALLBACK_ENV_DEFAULT substring only exists in review_autofix.yml; plan.yml and implement.yml use split formatting/comments, so the test does not model the real YAML.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1453 and 1598 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The retry loop and fallback guard both hardcode `3`.
  WHY: The reviewer said it is correct today but fragile if the loop bound changes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1599 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fallback guard uses hardcoded `3` instead of deriving from the loop bound.
  WHY: The code is correct today but fragile to future maintenance.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml, .github/workflows/plan.yml, scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: the three fallback-switch blocks | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No handling when the fallback model itself is invalid, unavailable, or rate-limited.
  WHY: The code echoes a message but continues execution with the fallback model regardless of whether it's viable.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py:62-68 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The contract test expects an exact multi-line YAML substring in all three workflow files, but plan.yml and implement.yml use split formatting with comments that do not contain this exact substring.
  WHY: pytest will fail in CI on every run because the exact string match cannot be satisfied by the actual YAML formatting.
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py:72-76 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test uses `assert text.count('CODEX_THREAD_REUSE_MODEL="${MODEL_EDITOR}"') == 1`, but implement.yml uses `CODEX_THREAD_REUSE_MODEL="${attempt_model}"`.
  WHY: The count assertion will fail, causing the test suite to fail on CI.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml + .github/workflows/plan.yml + scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: fallback model switch blocks | severity=major | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fallback-simulation code only emits an echo message when the fallback model is not equal to primary, but provides no retry-with-original, escalation path, or operator-visible error detection beyond the echo.
  WHY: If the fallback model itself is also invalid, unavailable, rate-limited, or removed from the catalog, the final attempt still fails with the same capacity error and there is no provisioned fallback.
- scripts/codex_model_catalog.json: lines 383-384 (priority field) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new openai/gpt-5.5 entry sets `"priority": 2`, while the nearby gpt-5.4 entry has `"priority": 10`. The copied base_instructions field also duplicates the system prompt content.
  WHY: Catalog priority can affect model selection in codex CLI paths and general model listing beyond the editor scope; a lower-priority entry may not be selected as expected.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: lines 1453 and 1600 (attempt loop vs fallback guard) | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Loop condition uses `while [ "${attempt}" -le 3 ]`, but fallback guard uses hardcoded `if [ "${attempt}" -ge 3 ]`, creating needless coupling between loop bounds and fallback logic.
  WHY: If someone modifies the loop bound in the future, the fallback behavior could silently drift or become misaligned without any change to the guard expression itself.
- TASK GAP
  Requirement: The contract test should reliably assert that the fallback environment variable is present and correctly formatted across all three workflow files, regardless of YAML formatting variations or comment placements.
  Expected change site: tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py
  Evidence of absence: The test expects an exact FALLBACK_ENV_DEFAULT YAML substring that does not exist in plan.yml or implement.yml due to split formatting and comments; review_autofix.yml contains the expected string.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: Line 1598 (fallback guard) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback trigger uses a hardcoded `-ge 3` check while the retry loop at line 1453 uses `-le 3`.
  WHY: If the loop bound is ever changed, the fallback guard would fire on attempts 3, 4, and 5 instead of only the final attempt.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: Line 426 (emit_editor_substate function) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The telemetry/ledger logging uses the raw MODEL_EDITOR variable instead of the per-attempt EDITOR_ATTEMPT_MODEL.
  WHY: Operational telemetry will incorrectly report the primary model was used when in fact the fallback model was active, making debugging capacity failures harder.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: line ~1600 (`[ "${attempt}" -ge 3 ]`) vs. line ~1453 (`while [ "${attempt}" -le 3 ]`) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback trigger is hardcoded to `3` while the loop bound is also hardcoded to `3` in a separate condition.
  WHY: If a future change raises the retry limit, the fallback switch would activate two attempts too early and defeat the design intent of preserving the primary model until the last attempt.
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py: `test_plan_loop_switches_model_on_final_attempt` and `test_review_apply_fixes_switches_model_on_final_attempt` | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both tests assert that `--model "${MODEL_EDITOR}"` is entirely absent, making them brittle to any additional legitimate codex invocation that intentionally uses the primary model.
  WHY: `pytest` fails on CI when a valid, unrelated change introduces another primary-model codex call.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- tests/test_editor_capacity_fallback_contract.py:60-100 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The contract test hard-codes both the exact FALLBACK_ENV_DEFAULT substring across all three workflows and the exact count of `CODEX_THREAD_REUSE_MODEL="${MODEL_EDITOR}"` in implement.yml.
  WHY: The reviewer said both assertions fail against the committed YAML and the count check only accounts for the repair pass.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1595-1603 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback guard uses `-ge 3` while the loop upper bound is hard-coded to 3, so the “final attempt only” contract is not expressed in terms of the loop limit.
  WHY: If the editor loop bound ever changes, the fallback switch could silently activate on the wrong attempt.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml (lines ~1178-1188), .github/workflows/implement.yml (lines ~2232-2242), scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh (lines ~1590-1604) | severity=major | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No validation, fallback-to-primary logic, or escalated logging exists if the fallback model itself is invalid, absent from the catalog, rate-limited, or returns an immediate error.
  WHY: The PR’s “ride out saturation” intent is only best-effort; if the fallback is also broken, execution continues into a broken state with no clear path forward.
- scripts/codex_model_catalog.json: new openai/gpt-5.5 entry (≈lines 364-398) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The entry mirrors gpt-5.4 fields but sets `"priority": 2`, and duplicates the long base_instructions string.
  WHY: Catalog priority influences model selection/listing in some codex-cli paths, so the lower priority may cause unexpected ordering or fallback behavior outside the explicit editor-retry use case.
